Two chords **intersect** if their endpoints alternate around the oriented circle. A chord is **isolated** if it intersects no other chord. The **1T relation** sets every unframed diagram with an isolated chord equal to zero. The framed degree-$n$ chord-diagram module is the free $R$-module on degree-$n$ chord diagrams modulo all 4T relations. The unframed degree-$n$ chord-diagram module is the free $R$-module on degree-$n$ chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T relations. A framed weight system is an $R$-linear functional on the framed module; an unframed weight system is an $R$-linear functional on the unframed module.

derivations.claim: A degree-$n$ chord diagram is a pairing of $2n$ cyclically ordered endpoints, so only finitely many such diagrams exist. A 4T relation is determined by a background diagram and finitely many endpoint positions, and a 1T relation by one diagram; hence there are finitely many relation vectors. By [F1], each has integer coefficients, so they form the rows of a finite integer matrix $A$. Write $A_n(F):=F^{C_n}/\operatorname{rowspan}_F(A)$ and $W_n(F):=\operatorname{Hom}_F(A_n(F),F)$. Since $k$ has characteristic zero, $\mathbb Q$ embeds in $k$. The rank of $A$ is unchanged by this field extension: a nonzero maximal minor over $\mathbb Q$ remains nonzero in $k$, while every larger minor that vanishes over $\mathbb Q$ still vanishes in $k$. Thus the row space over $k$ is the scalar extension of the rational row space, and $A_n(k)\cong A_n(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$.

The quotient is finite-dimensional, so extending a rational basis and its dual basis gives $W_n(k)\cong W_n(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$. If $n=0$, the sole diagram is the empty diagram and any weight system is its value $c\in k$; the constant invariant $V(K)=c$ has top symbol $c$. For $n>0$, choose a finite $\mathbb Q$-basis $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_d$ of $W_n(\mathbb Q)$; finite-dimensional row reduction chooses this basis without a choice axiom. By [F2], for each $i$ there is a rational-valued finite-type invariant $V_i$ with top symbol $\phi_i$. Write the given weight system as $W=\sum_{i=1}^d a_i\phi_i$ with $a_i\in k$, and define $V=\sum_{i=1}^d a_iV_i$, viewing each rational value in $k$. Linearity of the finite-difference operator gives top symbol $W$. If $W_n(\mathbb Q)=0$, the sum is empty and the zero invariant supplies the zero weight system.
